summary: The candidate genuinely fixes the exact partial-word revision and comma-spacing examples and passes focused regressions, but it only recognizes selected punctuation. Punctuation-only growth with a closing quote, Unicode ellipsis, or em dash emits a repeated full word and corrupts the monotonic prompt prefix, so the broad original contract is only partially fixed.

tests.what_was_measured: On the exact recorded base, confirmed source import path and reproduced both original failures: word revision emitted 'erpillar' and comma growth recorded 'hello world ,'.
At exact candidate commit, 31 focused state, serving-transcription, and audio-chunking tests passed.

At exact candidate commit, reported word/comma cases and normal append/rollback boundaries passed; independent closing-quote, Unicode-ellipsis, and em-dash punctuation-only growth cases failed with duplicated words in emitted_text.

gpu_execution.evidence: The defect and candidate are deterministic Python string-state logic. No GPU or model weights are required, and no GPU result is claimed.

remaining_counterexamples: 'hello world' -> 'hello world"' emits 'world"' and records 'hello world world"' instead of emitting '"' and recording 'hello world"'.
'hello world' -> 'hello world…' emits 'world…' and records 'hello world world…' instead of emitting '…' and recording 'hello world…'.
'hello world' -> 'hello world—' emits 'world—' and records 'hello world world—' instead of emitting '—' and recording 'hello world—'.
remaining_limitations: Review ran on x86_64 with Python 3.12.3, not the reporter's macOS arm64 environment; the reproduced logic is platform-independent Python.
No Qwen3-ASR weights or model inference were used.
No live HTTP SSE or realtime WebSocket server was launched; direct shared-state reproduction and focused existing serving tests were used.
No native source changed, so a native rebuild was not applicable.
The pre-existing documented whitespace-free CJK rollback limitation remains outside this candidate review.
